questions.question: What is the purpose of variables in the Service Catalog?

options.text: To define item options for end users and customize items to customer needs

explanation.correct: Service Catalog variables customize items to customer needs, like offering different operating systems for computers. They define the structure of catalog item forms using questions that may affect prices. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=d82da79047b35ad4ca332a81736d433f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Inventory tracking is a separate function from variables.
User account creation is handled in User Administration.
Notifications are configured separately from catalog variables.

source.excerpt: Service Catalog variables are global and customize items to customer needs, like offering different operating systems for computers.

questions.question: In the Knowledge Management workflow described by ServiceNow, who reviews a submitted article and either publishes it or sends it back for revisions?

options.text: The service desk agent who requested it

explanation.correct: In the sample workflow, a knowledge contributor creates or updates an article and submits it for review. The knowledge manager reviews it and either publishes it or sends it back for revisions. Knowledge managers also review retirement requests. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/exploring-knowledge-management.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The knowledge user requests, reads, and shares articles; they don't review submissions.
The requester doesn't approve publication.
The workflow assigns review to the knowledge manager, not only to admins.

source.excerpt: The knowledge manager reviews the article and either publishes it or sends it back to the knowledge contributor for revisions.

questions.question: What controls the publishing and retirement process for a knowledge article?

options.text: The workflows defined for the knowledge base that the article belongs to
A business rule on the kb_knowledge table that can't be changed

explanation.correct: The publishing and retirement processes for a knowledge article are controlled by workflows defined for its knowledge base. You can assign different workflows to each knowledge base, use a default workflow, or create your own. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/r_KnowledgeWorkflows.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Publishing and retirement are configurable per knowledge base through workflows.
Categories organize articles; they don't control publishing.
The author's role affects who can edit, not which publishing process applies.

source.excerpt: The publishing and retirement processes for a knowledge article are controlled by workflows defined for the knowledge base that the article belongs to.

questions.question: A knowledge base uses the Knowledge - Instant Publish workflow. What happens when a contributor publishes a draft article?

options.text: The article is published immediately without approval, or on the scheduled date if set to publish later
The article goes to In Review until a manager approves it
The article is sent to the Knowledge Feedback table

explanation.correct: Knowledge - Instant Publish immediately publishes a draft article without requiring approval, or publishes it on the scheduled publish date if it is set to publish later. Knowledge - Approval Publish requests approval from a knowledge base manager first. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/r_KnowledgeWorkflows.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: That describes Knowledge - Approval Publish.
Publishing doesn't retire articles.
The feedback table stores feedback, not articles being published.

source.excerpt: Immediately publishes a draft article without requiring an approval, or publishes on the scheduled publish date if set to publish later.

questions.question: With the Knowledge - Approval Publish workflow, what happens if the manager rejects the publish request?

options.text: The workflow is canceled and the article remains in Draft state
The article is published anyway after 24 hours

explanation.correct: Knowledge - Approval Publish requests approval from a knowledge base manager. Articles awaiting approval are In Review. If the manager rejects, the workflow is canceled and the article remains in Draft. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/r_KnowledgeWorkflows.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Rejected articles aren't published.
Rejection doesn't delete the article.
Retirement is a separate process.

source.excerpt: If the manager rejects the request, the workflow is canceled and the article remains in Draft state.

questions.question: A knowledge manager retires an outdated article and specifies a replacement article. What happens when a user opens the retired article?

options.text: They are automatically redirected to the replacement article with a message that the article was replaced
They see the retired article in read-only mode
They get an error and are logged out
Both articles open in separate tabs

explanation.correct: You can provide a replacement article when retiring an article. When the retired article is accessed, the user is redirected to the replacement with a message saying it was retired and replaced. Without a replacement, the page shows 'Knowledge record not found'. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/c_RetiredKnowledgeArticles.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Users are redirected rather than shown the retired article.
No logout occurs.
Only the replacement article opens.

source.excerpt: When the retired article is accessed, the user is automatically redirected to the replacement article

questions.question: Which roles can view retired knowledge articles?

options.text: All users with the knowledge role
Any user who rated the article

explanation.correct: Only administrators and knowledge administrators can view retired knowledge articles. To reuse a retired article, they can republish it. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/c_RetiredKnowledgeArticles.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The knowledge role doesn't give access to retired articles.
Rating an article doesn't grant access to it after retirement.
The documentation limits retired article visibility to admins and knowledge admins.

source.excerpt: Only administrators and knowledge administrators can view the retired knowledge articles.

questions.question: A knowledge base has a user criteria record in its Can Contribute related list. What access do matching users get?

options.text: They can create, modify, and retire articles, and they also get read access to all articles in the knowledge base
They can only comment on articles
They can administer all knowledge bases

explanation.correct: Can Contribute lets users create, modify, and retire articles in the knowledge base. Contribute access also provides read access to all articles in that knowledge base. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_SelectUserCriteria.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Can Contribute gives more than read access.
Commenting is feedback, not contribute access.
User criteria apply to a specific knowledge base, not to all of them.

documentation.section: Control access at the knowledge base level through user criteria

source.excerpt: Contribute access to a knowledge base also provides read access to all articles in the knowledge base.

questions.question: Which feedback options can users give on a knowledge article? (Choose three.)

options.text: Flag the article as incorrect or inappropriate
Mark the article as helpful or not helpful

explanation.correct: Users can flag an article, give it a rating, mark it helpful or not helpful, and view, add, or reply to comments. Knowledge managers view other feedback under Knowledge > Feedback. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/r_KnowledgeFeedback.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Moving an article to another knowledge base is not a feedback option.
Approving publication is part of the publishing workflow, not user feedback.

source.excerpt: Flag an article as incorrect or inappropriate. … Provide a rating value for the article. … Mark an article as helpful or not helpful.

questions.question: With article versioning enabled, how is a knowledge article number displayed?

options.text: With the version number, for example KB0010003 v2.0
With the author's user ID appended
With the knowledge base name as a prefix

explanation.correct: With article versioning, the knowledge article number includes the version number, for example KB0010003 v2.0. Contributors create new versions from a published version, and the existing version stays unchanged. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/article-versioning.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Article numbers are human-readable numbers, not sys_ids.
The author ID isn't part of the number.
The knowledge base name isn't used as a prefix.

source.excerpt: For example, KB0010003 v2.0.

questions.question: Which are basic Service Catalog item types? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: The basic Service Catalog item types are standard catalog items, record producers, order guides, and content items. Content items provide information instead of goods or services. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_IntroductionToCatalogItems.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Transform maps are used for importing data.
Business rules are server-side scripts.

source.excerpt: Record producers: Provide alternative ways … Order guides: Enable grouping multiple catalog items in one request. … Content Items: These are the catalog items which provide information instead of goods or services.

questions.question: An organization wants employees to report broken equipment by creating Incident records through a friendly catalog form rather than the standard incident form. What should the administrator create?

explanation.correct: A record producer is a type of catalog item that lets end users create task-based records, such as incidents, from the service catalog. It looks like a catalog item but generates a task record instead of a requested item. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: An order guide groups several catalog items into one request.
A content item provides information, not a record.
A variable set groups reusable variables; it doesn't generate records by itself.

source.excerpt: A record producer is a specific type of catalog item that allows end users to create task-based records, such as incident records, from the service catalog.

questions.question: Why should you avoid using a record producer to create requested item (RITM) records?

options.text: Standard catalog processes, such as starting the expected workflows, might not run; create requested items with catalog items instead
Record producers can't write to any task table
Record producers only work in Core UI

explanation.correct: Use a record producer to create task-based records only. To make sure standard Service Catalog processes run as expected, such as starting workflows, don't create requested item records from record producers. Create them with catalog items. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Record producers do create task-based records such as incidents.
Record producers aren't limited to Core UI.
Record producers are a current catalog item type.

source.excerpt: do not create requested item records from record producers. Instead, create requested item using catalog items.

questions.question: An order guide for new hires asks for the employee's location once and then orders a laptop, phone, and business cards. How is the location passed to the ordered items?

options.text: By copying the order guide record

explanation.correct: An order guide submits one request that generates several items, based on order guide rule conditions. Information entered in the order guide can be passed as cascading variables to the ordered items so common data is reused. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogOrderGuides.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Transform maps are for data imports.
A scheduled job isn't how order guide data reaches items.
Cascading variables pass the data, not a copy of the order guide.

source.excerpt: Information the customer enters within the order guide can be passed as cascading variables to the ordered items

questions.question: How does an order guide decide which catalog items to order?

options.text: By evaluating order guide rule conditions
By always ordering every item in the catalog
By asking a fulfiller to pick items

explanation.correct: Order guides determine which catalog items to order by evaluating order guide rule conditions against the information the customer provides. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogOrderGuides.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Items are added based on rule conditions, not all items.
Items are chosen automatically by rules.
Favorites don't drive order guide rules.

source.excerpt: Order guides determine which catalog items to order by evaluating order guide rule conditions.

questions.question: A catalog administrator must add the same five questions to 10 server catalog items and wants future changes to apply to all of them. What should they use?

options.text: A separate variable on each item

explanation.correct: Variable sets are collections of variables that can be reused across multiple catalog items and order guides. When you modify the variable set, the change is reflected in every associated item. Variable sets can also include catalog client scripts and UI policies. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogVariableSets.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Adding variables item by item is repetitive and error-prone, which variable sets avoid.
Categories organize items; they don't hold variables.
A record producer creates task records; it doesn't share variables across items.

source.excerpt: Variable sets allow you to create a collection of variables that can be reused across multiple catalog items and order guides.

questions.question: Which role can create a variable set?

options.text: Catalog administrator (catalog_admin) or admin; catalog managers and editors can only attach existing variable sets
Any user with the itil role

explanation.correct: Administrators and catalog administrators define variable sets. Catalog managers and catalog editors can attach a variable set to items they are assigned to, but they cannot create a variable set. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogVariableSets.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Catalog editors can attach, but not create, variable sets.
Catalog managers can attach, but not create, variable sets.
The itil role doesn't grant catalog administration.

source.excerpt: However, catalog managers and catalog editors cannot create a variable set.

questions.question: A 'USA IT Hardware' catalog category should be visible only to sales staff based in the USA. What is the recommended way to restrict it?

options.text: Create a user criteria record matching those users and apply it to the category
Create an ACL on the sc_category table for each user
Hide the category with a UI policy
Put the category in a separate update set

explanation.correct: Administrators control access to catalog items and categories by creating user criteria records and applying them. For example, a USA Sales user criteria record can be applied to the USA IT Hardware category so only matching users can access it. Available For and Not Available For lists allow or prohibit access. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogAccessControls.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: User criteria is the Service Catalog access mechanism for items and categories.
UI policies control form behavior, not catalog visibility.
Update sets move configuration; they don't restrict access.

documentation.section: Set security for items and categories

source.excerpt: An administrator can control access to content in the service catalog by creating and applying user criteria records.

questions.question: A category has no active catalog items anywhere in its hierarchy. What happens to it?

options.text: It doesn't appear in the catalog and can't be added to the catalog
It shows as an empty category
It is moved to the parent catalog

explanation.correct: If there are no active items in a category's hierarchy, that category doesn't appear in the catalog and can't be added to the catalog. A catalog item can exist in multiple categories. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogCategories.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Categories without active items are not displayed.
The category isn't deleted.
The category isn't moved.

source.excerpt: If there are no active items in a category’s hierarchy, that category does not appear in the catalog, and cannot be added to the catalog.

questions.question: A catalog UI policy is applied to a variable set and a different action is applied to the catalog item. By default, which takes precedence?

options.text: The UI policy for the catalog item
The UI policy for the variable set

explanation.correct: The UI policy for catalog items always takes precedence over the UI policy for variable sets. This behavior can be changed with the glide.sc.ui_policy.variable_set_run_first property. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogUIPolicy.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Variable set policies run second by default.
Creation date doesn't decide precedence.
Both policies run; the item policy takes precedence.

source.excerpt: The UI policy for catalog items always takes precedence over UI policy for variable sets.

questions.question: Where can service catalog variable values be displayed after an item has been ordered? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Variables capture information the customer provides when ordering. They can be passed between tasks during fulfillment and displayed on the Requested Item and Catalog Task forms after the item is ordered. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogVariables.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Variables are not shown on user profiles.
Variables are not written to the system log for display.
The Schema Map shows table relationships.

source.excerpt: They can be displayed on the Requested Item and Catalog Task forms after an item has been ordered.

questions.question: According to Service Catalog guidance, which of these can be a catalog item?

options.text: A high-resolution display that only exists as part of a laptop
A field on the incident form

explanation.correct: Anything that can be ordered on its own can be a catalog item. Something that only exists as part of a larger whole can't. A laptop can be a catalog item, but a high-resolution display for a laptop cannot. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_UsingTheServiceCatalog.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Parts of a larger whole are not catalog items in themselves.
Form fields aren't orderable goods or services.
Roles are security settings, not catalog items.

documentation.section: Service Catalog for managers and end users

source.excerpt: For example, a laptop can be a catalog item, but a high-resolution display for a laptop cannot.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Catalog Builder?

options.text: To delegate the creation and maintenance of catalog items through a visual, guided experience with restrictions
To import catalog items from spreadsheets

explanation.correct: Catalog Builder lets you delegate the creation and maintenance of catalog items. You can create or edit catalog items and record producers in a visual, guided experience with restrictions, and create templates for new items. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-builder-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Catalog Builder is a guided editor, not an import tool.
Portal pages are designed with portal tools, not Catalog Builder.
Approvals are built in Workflow Studio.

source.excerpt: The Catalog Builder experience enables you to delegate the creation and maintenance of catalog items.

questions.question: Which three components make up a flow in Workflow Studio?

options.text: A trigger, a sequence of reusable actions, and flow logic
A table, a form, and a list
A client script, a UI policy, and an ACL
An import set, a transform map, and a data source

explanation.correct: A flow is an automated process made of a trigger, a sequence of reusable actions, and flow logic. The trigger specifies when the flow runs and the actions perform operations on your data. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-flows.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Tables, forms, and lists are data and UI elements.
Client scripts, UI policies, and ACLs are form and security configuration.
These are components for importing data.

source.excerpt: A flow is an automated process consisting of a trigger, a sequence of reusable actions, and flow logic.

questions.question: How does a subflow differ from a flow?

options.text: A subflow has no trigger; it runs when called from a flow, another subflow, or a script
A subflow can only run on a schedule
A subflow can't have inputs or outputs
A subflow runs only in the browser

explanation.correct: Subflows are sequences of reusable actions with inputs and outputs. Unlike flows, subflows have no trigger and run when called from a flow, another subflow, or a script. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-flows.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Scheduled triggers belong to flows; subflows have no trigger.
Subflows have inputs and outputs.
Subflows run on the server like flows.

source.excerpt: In contrast to flows, subflows do not have a trigger but instead run when called from a flow, from another subflow, or from a script.

questions.question: Which trigger categories do flows support? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Flows support record-based, schedule-based, and application-based trigger types. The trigger defines when the flow starts and the starting data available to it. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-flows.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: onChange is a client script type, not a flow trigger category.
There is no dictionary-based flow trigger category.

source.excerpt: Flows support record-based, schedule-based, and application-based trigger types.

questions.question: A flow has an Updated record trigger. The process should run only one time over the whole life of each record. Which run option should the flow author select?

explanation.correct: For Updated or Created or Updated record triggers, Once triggers the flow once for the life of the record. The documentation also notes that flows with approval actions should only run the trigger once. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-triggers.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: For each unique change runs for every unique update, even while the flow is running.
For every update runs every time the record is updated.
Only if not currently running runs on each unique change when the flow isn't already running on that record.

source.excerpt: Once: Triggers the flow once for the life of the record.

questions.question: Which statement about scheduled flow triggers is correct?

options.text: They use the instance time zone, and the flow may not start at the exact scheduled time because flows are processed asynchronously
They use each user's personal time zone
They always run at the exact second scheduled

explanation.correct: Scheduled triggers start a flow at a date and time or at intervals (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Run Once, Repeat). They use the instance time zone. Because flows are processed asynchronously, a scheduled flow may not run at the exact scheduled time. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-triggers.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The instance time zone is used, not user time zones.
Asynchronous processing means the exact time isn't guaranteed.
Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Repeat triggers run more than once.

source.excerpt: Scheduled triggers use the instance timezone to determine when to start a flow. … a flow with a scheduled trigger may not run at the exact scheduled time

questions.question: A flow author has built and tested a flow. What else must happen before it runs when its trigger conditions are met?

options.text: The flow must be added to an update set
The flow must be converted to a subflow
A catalog item must be created for it

explanation.correct: After testing a flow, you activate it to make it available to run. Only activated flows run when their trigger conditions are met or when called by a script. Activating requires write access, with the flow_designer or admin role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-activate.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Update sets capture changes for migration; they don't make a flow run.
Subflows have no trigger, so converting would stop it from triggering.
Catalog items aren't needed for a record-triggered flow.

source.excerpt: Only activated flows run when their trigger conditions are met or when called by a script.

questions.question: A flow must apply the same actions to every record in a list returned by a Look Up Records action. Which flow logic should the author use?

options.text: Wait for a duration of time

explanation.correct: For each flow logic applies one or more actions to each record in a list of records. If applies actions only when conditions are met, Wait for a duration pauses the flow, and End Flow stops it. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-logic.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: If applies actions conditionally; it doesn't loop.
Wait for a duration pauses the flow.
End Flow stops the flow.

source.excerpt: Apply one or more actions to each record in a list of records.

questions.question: A process has many conditional paths, and nested If / Else If blocks are becoming hard to maintain. Which flow logic does ServiceNow offer as an alternative?

options.text: Make a decision, which uses decision table branching logic

explanation.correct: Make a decision uses decision table branching logic when multiple conditional paths are required, as an alternative to nested If, Else If, or Else flow logic. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-logic.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Parallel logic runs paths at the same time; it doesn't choose between them.
Set Flow Variables assigns values to variables.
Call a Workflow runs a legacy workflow.

source.excerpt: as an alternative to nested If, Else If, or Else flow logic.

questions.question: What is a spoke in Workflow Studio?

options.text: A scoped application containing Workflow Studio actions and subflows for managing specific tables or systems
A trigger that runs every hour

explanation.correct: A spoke is a scoped application that contains Workflow Studio actions and subflows. For example, the ITSM Spoke has actions for managing Incident and Problem records. More spokes can be activated from the ServiceNow Store or by activating plugins. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-flows.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Spokes contain actions and subflows; they aren't triggers.
Spokes are not catalog variables.
Spokes are not database objects.

source.excerpt: A spoke is a scoped application containing Workflow Studio actions and subflows for managing specific tables.

questions.question: What is the benefit of a saved trigger in Workflow Studio?

options.text: Flow authors can reuse a predefined trigger, and changes to it are propagated to every flow that uses it
It runs faster than a normal trigger
It is the only trigger type that works with catalog items
It removes the need to activate the flow

explanation.correct: A saved trigger lets flow authors use a predefined trigger instead of building a new one for each flow. Any changes made to the saved trigger are propagated to each flow that uses it. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/building-triggers.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Performance isn't the documented benefit.
Catalog requests have their own trigger types.
Flows still need to be activated.

source.excerpt: Any changes made to the trigger are propagated to each flow that uses the trigger.

questions.question: Which types of workflow items can you create from the Workflow Studio homepage? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: From one interface, Workflow Studio lets you work with playbooks, flows, subflows, actions, data stream actions, and decision tables. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-workflow-studio.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import sets are created with System Import Sets, not Workflow Studio.
UI policies are form configuration, not Workflow Studio items.

source.excerpt: Options include playbooks, flows, subflows, actions, data stream actions, and decision tables.

questions.question: What does ServiceNow Virtual Agent provide?

options.text: User assistance through conversations in an intelligent messaging interface
A tool to design database schemas

explanation.correct: The Virtual Agent platform provides user assistance through conversations within an intelligent messaging interface. It helps users get information, make decisions, and perform common tasks, which frees agents for more complex issues. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/conversational-interfaces/virtual-agent/exploring-virtual-agent.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Schema design isn't a Virtual Agent function.
Report scheduling is part of reporting.
Form layout is configured with Form Builder.

source.excerpt: The ServiceNow Virtual Agent platform provides user assistance through conversations within an intelligent messaging interface.

questions.question: Which version of Virtual Agent is automatically included with the ServiceNow AI Platform?

options.text: Virtual Agent Lite, a limited version
No version; Virtual Agent must be built from scratch

explanation.correct: Virtual Agent is available as a professional subscription or as a limited version, Virtual Agent Lite, which is automatically included with the ServiceNow AI Platform. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/conversational-interfaces/virtual-agent/exploring-virtual-agent.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Virtual Agent Professional is a subscription.
This is not a documented Virtual Agent edition.
A limited version is included by default.

source.excerpt: a limited version (Virtual Agent Lite) that is automatically included with the ServiceNow AI Platform

questions.question: What are Virtual Agent conversations built from?

explanation.correct: Virtual Agent conversations are built using topics. When building a topic you use controls to define the conversation logic and the responses the user sees. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/conversational-interfaces/virtual-agent/conversation-designer-virtual-agent.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Transform maps are for importing data.
Business rules are server-side scripts on tables.
Report sources are predefined data sets for reports.

documentation.section: Getting started with the Asset library in Assistant Designer

source.excerpt: Virtual Agent conversations are built using topics.

questions.question: In NLU topic discovery for Virtual Agent, what is an intent?

options.text: A description of what the user wants to achieve, which user utterances are matched against to pick the topic
A list of keywords that must appear exactly
The role required to use the chat

explanation.correct: With NLU/keyword topic discovery, the topic author associates a topic with an intent in an NLU model. An intent describes what the user wants to achieve, and user utterances are matched with intents to find the most appropriate topic. Associating a topic with a model and intent is called mapping. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/conversational-interfaces/virtual-agent/conversation-designer-virtual-agent.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Exact keyword lists are what natural language models improve on.
Themes and branding are chat configuration, not intents.
Intents aren't security roles.

documentation.section: Getting started with the Asset library in Assistant Designer

source.excerpt: An intent describes what the user wants to achieve.

questions.question: Which role, besides admin, is listed for using Virtual Agent Designer to build and test conversations?

explanation.correct: Virtual Agent Designer lets you build and test conversations without scripting by dragging elements onto a graphical canvas. The listed roles are virtual_agent_admin or admin. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/conversational-interfaces/virtual-agent/exploring-virtual-agent.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: catalog_admin administers the Service Catalog.
knowledge_manager manages knowledge bases.
report_admin administers reports.

source.excerpt: virtual_agent_admin or admin

questions.question: A flow should keep running and run a set of recovery actions if an error occurs inside a group of actions. Which flow logic should the author use?

explanation.correct: Try flow logic lets a flow keep running when an error occurs inside a flow logic block and runs a sequence of actions in response to errors in that block. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-logic.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: End Flow stops the flow.
Do the following until repeats actions until a condition is met.
Set Flow Variables assigns values to flow variables.

source.excerpt: Allow a flow to continue running when an error occurs within a flow logic block.

questions.question: A company wants to offer the same laptop catalog item under both the Hardware and New Hire categories. Is this possible?

options.text: Yes, a catalog item can exist in multiple categories
No, each item belongs to exactly one category
Only if the item is copied into a second item

explanation.correct: A catalog item can exist in multiple categories, so you can offer the same service from several places in the catalog. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogCategories.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Items aren't limited to one category.
Copying isn't needed.
Order guides group items for one request; they aren't needed for categorization.

source.excerpt: A catalog item can exist in multiple categories

questions.question: What is a Variable Set in ServiceNow?

options.text: A container that groups variables together, saving time and reducing errors

explanation.correct: Instead of adding variables to each item separately, Variable Sets group them, saving time and reducing errors. Updates to a Variable Set apply to all associated items. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=d82da79047b35ad4ca332a81736d433f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Roles are managed separately and are not related to Variable Sets.
Reports are created in the reporting module, not Variable Sets.
Backup mechanisms are system-level functions, not Variable Sets.

source.excerpt: Instead of adding variables to each item separately, Variable Sets group them, saving time and reducing errors. Updates to a Variable Set apply to all associated items.

questions.question: What is a Record Producer in ServiceNow?

options.text: A catalog item that creates task-based records more easily than using a standard form

explanation.correct: A Record Producer in ServiceNow is a catalog item that lets users create task-based records, like incidents, more easily than using a standard form. It appears similar to other catalog items but generates task records instead. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=d82da79047b35ad4ca332a81736d433f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Record Producers create records, not backup them.
Workflows are separate from Record Producers.
Dashboards are for reporting, not record creation.

source.excerpt: A Record Producer in ServiceNow is a catalog item that lets users create task-based records, like incidents, more easily than using a standard form.

questions.question: What is an Order Guide used for?

options.text: To let users request multiple related items at once

explanation.correct: Order Guides let users request multiple related items at once and help them decide what they need, with variables arranged by order number. Items must be complete with variables and a delivery flow before being added to an Order Guide. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=d82da79047b35ad4ca332a81736d433f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User manuals are documentation, not Order Guides.
Shipping is handled separately from Order Guides.
Inventory management is a different function.

source.excerpt: Order Guides let users request multiple related items at once and help them decide what they need, with variables arranged by order number.

questions.question: What happens if no user criteria is set on a knowledge base's 'can read' related list?

options.text: All users can read it, and all users with roles can contribute to it
Only the knowledge manager can view articles

explanation.correct: If no user criteria are selected for a knowledge base, all users can read it and all users with roles can contribute to it. Use Can Read and Can Contribute user criteria to restrict access. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/user-access-knowledge.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Without criteria, access is open to all, not restricted to admins.
The knowledge base remains active, just publicly accessible.
Without restrictions, all users can view, not just managers.

documentation.section: Managing access to knowledge bases and knowledge articles

source.excerpt: If no user criteria is selected for a knowledge base, all users can read and all users with roles can contribute to that knowledge base.

questions.question: How can users provide feedback on knowledge articles?

options.text: By commenting or flagging articles, which notifies kb administrators

explanation.correct: Users can provide feedback by commenting or flagging articles, which notifies kb administrators. This helps maintain quality and allows users to participate in knowledge improvement. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=9e8c67dc47735ad4ca332a81736d43ad&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Users typically cannot delete articles; that's an admin function.
Category creation is an administrative task.
Workflow modification requires admin access.

source.excerpt: Users can also provide feedback by commenting or flagging articles, which notifies kb administrators.

questions.question: Which user criteria types are used to control access to knowledge bases? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Knowledge bases use user criteria including: can read/can't read, and can contribute/can't contribute. These control who can view articles and who can create or edit them. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=9e8c67dc47735ad4ca332a81736d43ad&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Delete permissions are managed separately, not through user criteria.
Export permissions are not standard user criteria options.

source.excerpt: User criteria include can read, can't read; can contribute, can't contribute.

questions.question: In the Service Catalog request structure, what does each catalog item within a request have?

options.text: Multiple tasks that are specific to that item
Shared tasks with all other items

explanation.correct: In a Service Catalog request, each item can have several tasks. Even if tasks have similar names, they are specific to each item because the steps for each may vary. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=d82da79047b35ad4ca332a81736d433f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Items can have multiple tasks, not just one.
Items typically have tasks for fulfillment in addition to approvals.
Tasks are specific to each item, not shared across items.

source.excerpt: In a Service Catalog, a request can include multiple items, and each item can have several tasks... Even if tasks have similar names, they are specific to each item, because the steps for each may vary.

questions.question: Where can users track their submitted service requests?

explanation.correct: After submitting a request, users can track it through All > Self-Service > My Requests. Flow stages show the progress of an item with stages. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=d82da79047b35ad4ca332a81736d433f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: System Logs are for technical logging, not user request tracking.
This is not the correct navigation path for user requests.
Reports provide analytics, not individual request tracking.

source.excerpt: After submitting a request, users can track it through All, Self-Service, My Requests.

questions.question: What is the purpose of categories in Knowledge Management?

options.text: To help organize knowledge bases and make articles easier to find

explanation.correct: Categories help organize knowledge bases and make articles easier to find. Knowledge managers define categories, while contributors can select and modify them if allowed. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=9e8c67dc47735ad4ca332a81736d43ad&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User account creation is in User Administration.
Workflow approvals are managed separately.
Notifications are configured in System Notification.

source.excerpt: Categories help organize knowledge bases and make articles easier to find.

questions.question: What determines the order in which variables are displayed on a catalog item form?

options.text: The order field value - lower numbers show first

explanation.correct: The order field sets the display sequence for variables. Lower numbers show first, allowing administrators to control the logical flow of questions on catalog item forms. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=d82da79047b35ad4ca332a81736d433f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Variables are ordered by the order field, not alphabetically.
Creation date doesn't determine display order.
Order is explicitly configured, not random.

source.excerpt: The order field sets display sequence. Lower numbers show first.

questions.question: What can users do in the Service Portal? (Choose two.)

options.text: Search knowledge bases and browse catalogs

explanation.correct: Service Portal allows users to search knowledge bases, browse catalogs, make requests, create and view incidents, and check system status. It's designed for end-user self-service, not administration. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=9e8c67dc47735ad4ca332a81736d43ad&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Security settings require admin access, not available in Service Portal.
Database schema changes require admin access and specialized tools.

source.excerpt: Service Portal allows users to search knowledge bases, browse catalogs, make requests, create and view incidents, and check system status.

questions.question: Which are core actions available in Workflow Studio? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Core actions in Workflow Studio include Ask For Approval, Create Record, Delete Record, Lookup Record, and Wait for Condition. Additional application-specific actions are available through spokes. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-record-flow-designer.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Send SMS is not listed as a core action in Workflow Studio.
Generate PDF is not a core Workflow Studio action.

source.excerpt: Available as a Workflow Studio ServiceNow core action.

questions.question: What does the 'match all' checkbox control on a knowledge base's user criteria?

options.text: Whether all articles in the knowledge base require approval
Whether all criteria must match (checked) or any criteria grants access (unchecked)
Whether all users can contribute to the knowledge base
Whether all knowledge bases share the same user criteria

explanation.correct: The 'match all' checkbox determines access: when checked, all criteria must match for access; when unchecked, matching any criteria grants access. By default, it is unchecked. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/create-user-criteria-record-in-knowledge-management.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The 'match all' checkbox controls user criteria matching, not article approval.
Contribution access is controlled by 'can contribute' user criteria, not the 'match all' checkbox.
Each knowledge base has its own user criteria settings.

documentation.section: Create user criteria for controlling access to knowledge bases and articles

source.excerpt: If selected, only users who match all user criteria are given access. If cleared, the user must meet one or more of the set user criteria to be given access.

questions.question: What is the correct order of records created when a user submits a Service Catalog request?

explanation.correct: The Service Catalog creates a Request (sc_request) which contains one or more Requested Items (sc_req_item/RITM), which may generate Catalog Tasks (sc_task) for fulfillment. This is the standard three-tier request model. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RequestingAServiceCatalogItem.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incidents are not created as part of the standard catalog request process.
The order is reversed — Requests are created first, not Catalog Tasks.
Change Requests are separate from the catalog request process.

source.excerpt: When a customer orders something from the catalog, a request is generated to track the order. … Each individual catalog item that is part of a request creates a discrete request item with the request.
